GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2015-07-28T13:30:22Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Common generic parameter type inference doesn't work for derived parameter types
Description: Consider following definitions:

```
class BaseClass<T> {
}

class DerivedClass extends BaseClass<number> {
}

function usingParameters<T>(c:BaseClass<T>, p:T) {
}
```

In `usingParameters(new BaseClass<number>(), "string")` call common type inference works well and as a result can't infer common generic parameter type and compiler fails with error.

In `usingParameters(new DerivedClass(), "string");` call common type inference doesn't seem to check if `DerivedClass` derives exactly from `BaseClass<string>` or that `"string"` is not `number` and everything compiles well.

The same thing about object notation

```
interface IParameters<T> {
    c: BaseClass<T>,
    p: T
}

function usingObject<T>(IParameters<T>) {
}

usingObject({ c: new BaseClass<number>(), p: "string" }); //Fails
usingObject({ c: new DerivedClass(), p: "string" }); //Compiles
```
